What does one event actually tell you about the scene?
One way to say it
A pixel reports that its log brightness has changed by a threshold since its last reset. The event gives the location, time, and sign of that change. It measures a relative change; both motion and changing illumination can produce it.
Keep these ideas
threshold crossing · local reference · motion or illumination
If pressed

The ideal rule uses fixed contrast thresholds. Threshold variation and other sensor errors enter the observation-model discussion.

Why do events leave a brightness baseline undetermined?
One way to say it
Adding a constant to a pixel's entire log-brightness history preserves all its changes, provided its reset reference shifts with it. The temporal difference model therefore determines the history only up to an additive level. The regularizer chooses that level; a measured reference could supply physical information about it.

Independent per-pixel offsets in log intensity correspond to independent multiplicative brightness factors after exponentiation.

One way to say it
It gives an estimate that exists, is unique, and changes continuously with the specified inputs. That makes the model's answer determinate and controlled. Accuracy also depends on whether the observations identify the physical quantity and whether the model's assumptions and regularization describe the scene well.

What do the temporal kernels change, and what do they preserve?
One way to say it
A kernel distributes an event's signed contribution across time bins. Unit mass preserves its total contribution when the full support is included, while the width controls how far the influence spreads. The difference operator stays fixed; the observations and any weights derived from them can change.

A kernel crossing the observation-window boundary needs boundary treatment to preserve the full mass identity.

Why is the cumulative event signal naturally BV rather than H-one?
One way to say it
Accumulating finitely many signed events gives a staircase with finite total variation. A nonzero jump contributes an atom to its distributional derivative. H-one would require a square-integrable derivative, so a genuine jump belongs naturally in bounded variation instead.
Keep these ideas

If pressed

At positive smoothing width, the kernels used here give a square-integrable driver and an H-one primitive.

One way to say it
With one scalar penalty, the temporal modes diagonalize the reconstruction map. The data leave the constant mode free, and the penalty selects zero for it. Slow nonconstant modes are reduced most, while faster modes retain more of their latent amplitude. That explains the emphasis on changing structure in the reconstruction.

For a mode with difference-energy eigenvalue g, the latent gain is g/(g + lambda squared). General diagonal penalties need matrix analysis.

How would you explain regularization bias to the committee?
One way to say it
The penalty deliberately pulls the estimate toward smaller profiles. Even with exact increments, that changes the recovered nonconstant modes and fixes the invisible baseline. Reconstruction error therefore contains both this shrinkage bias and propagated observation error; increasing regularization trades more shrinkage for stronger noise control.
Keep these ideas

If pressed

On a fixed grid, noiseless mean-zero latent profiles are recovered as the scalar penalty tends to zero. The missing constant still requires a convention.

What is actually computed after you write down the temporal objective?
One way to say it
Differentiating gives one positive-definite linear system per pixel. We solve those independent systems in parallel to obtain temporal histories. At any reconstruction time, taking that time sample from each history assembles an image. The optimization variable is the whole history, even though the output is displayed as frames.
Keep these ideas
normal equations · independent pixel solves · assemble time slices
If pressed

I developed and used a native C++/CUDA DV version for live windowed reconstruction. Workload, temporal samples, observation window, and output cadence govern responsiveness; fine event timestamps and camera-to-display latency are different quantities.

One way to say it
Instead of fitting each pixel history independently, we ask one static scene to explain observations along a known camera trajectory. We project that scene at each time and then difference the projections. A positive ridge makes the fixed-motion scene solve unique and stable, while the projection sequence determines its invisible scene directions.
Keep these ideas

If pressed

SAR means synthetic aperture radar. Here the transferred idea is combining moving-sensor observations into one scene estimate; camera motion is supplied to the model.

What directional information does the structure tensor add?
One way to say it
It pools outer products of nearby space-time gradients with nonnegative weights. Each contribution is a squared directional constraint, so the tensor is positive semidefinite. Nonparallel spatial gradients can constrain both velocity components locally; the unified theorem only requires enough information across the connected domain.
Keep these ideas

If pressed

Its spatial block supplies data curvature, the space-time cross terms supply forcing, and the final temporal term is constant in velocity.

What happens in one block-Jacobi sweep for the discrete flow model?
One way to say it
Every pixel solves a local two-component system combining its directional data with its neighbors' previous velocities. All updates use the same old field, and then the whole field is replaced at once. Under the stated graph and sampled-information assumptions, repeating these sweeps converges to the unique discrete minimizer.
Keep these ideas

If pressed

The assumptions include positive smoothing, positive node factors and degrees, symmetric nonnegative edge weights, connected positive-weight support, PSD data blocks, and a positive-definite weighted sum of those blocks.

Which next research questions follow directly from your results?
One way to say it
For flow, quantify how raw-event errors become coefficient errors. For adaptive reconstruction, control the full weight-update map and its sensitivity. For stereo, extend the candidate-margin analysis to the weighted aggregated score. Controlled common-pixel comparisons would help connect those mathematical refinements to physical accuracy.
Keep these ideas
representation error · full adaptive map · implemented stereo margins

Learned temporal regularization can start from the smooth fixed-positive-weight solution map. Shared-scene sensing can start from trajectory-dependent invariant modes.
